subject: Re: Veridian MAP — Performance benchmarking playbook & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@veridianhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Veridian MAP kickoff: perf scope & timelines

Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed, Veridian is ready to move forward with a short MAP focused on performance verification for our clinical triage workflow. High level ask: we need a clear benchmarking plan (workload, SLOs, test harness) and a timeline that lines up with our procurement cadence (contract signature target 2026-11-12).

Key context:
- Peak concurrent inference expected ~200–300 parallel user sessions (bursty during clinic hours).
- Typical prompt lengths vary 40–300 tokens; 99% of requests are < 600 tokens.
- TTFT is a strong customer KPI for UX; they want first token < 250ms for interactive routes.

Can you share a playbook with proposed workload profiles, acceptance criteria (latency percentiles, throughput, TTFT), and a proposed 2-week execution plan we can include in the MAP doc? Also include what artifacts you need from us to run the benchmark (sample payloads, auth, network topology).

Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
Veridian Health
[Attachment: veridian_initial_capacity_plan.xlsx]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Veridian MAP kickoff: perf scope & timelines

Tom — thanks, this is helpful. Attached is a draft playbook (veridian_map_v1.xlsx) that covers: workload profiles, success criteria, SLOs, test harness design, and a proposed 10-business-day execution timeline that finishes with a results review. Highlights below so you can quickly see the acceptance gates.

Workload profiles (short):
- Interactive (priority): 1–4 concurrent tokens streamed; target median TTFT <= 160ms; p99 first-token <= 250ms; sustained concurrency test at 250 rps for 15 minutes (burst to 400 rps).
- Batch (background summarization): larger payloads up to 3k tokens; throughput measured in tokens/sec; target 95th percentile processing latency <= 5s for batches of 1–5 concurrent jobs.
- Mixed day-long trace: replay of ~200k historical events across a 24h window to validate autoscaling and cache effectiveness.

Success criteria (must pass to sign-off):
- Interactive route: p99 latency (first token) <= 300ms in production-like network; median TTFT <= 180ms; error rate < 0.5%.
- Throughput: achieve >= 250 sustained rps at the interactive profile without SLO violations for 15 minutes.
- Concurrency/scale: autoscaling recovers to baseline throughput within 90s of a 3x load spike.
- Regression checks: sample prompt set evaluation shows <= 1.5% degraded output quality vs baseline (we'll run evals).

Test harness notes:
- We will run from a Redwood Private staging cluster in the same cloud region you plan to use (us-west-2).
- Need: sample payload JSONs (we used load_profile_samples.json), an allowlist IP for our load agents, and a short-term API key scoped to the MAP tests.

Timeline (proposed):
- Day 0–1: kickoff & artifact handoff (you deliver payloads + allowlist + SLA expectations).
- Day 2–4: smoke runs and calibrate load generator; iterate on model/config.
- Day 5–7: full throughput & concurrency windows; capture detailed traces.
- Day 8–9: evals for quality/regression checks.
- Day 10: results review & MAP sign-off (deliver results_summary_20261103.csv + playbook updates).

I'll loop in Karthik for the harness details and Lauren for rollouts/ops acceptance. Let me know if this aligns with your procurement dates — we can shift testing earlier if you can provision sample traffic sooner.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: veridian_map_v1.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Veridian MAP kickoff: perf scope & timelines (internal)

Internal notes / checklist for execution:
- Load agents: use our filtered-agent set in us-west-2 (avoid EU agents to match Veridian).
- KV cache priming: create a 30-minute warmup window for interactive prompts to capture typical prefix reuse. Document warmup script in the playbook sheet "warmup.sh".
- Metrics to collect: first-token latency (p50,p95,p99), TTFT (median), tokens/sec, model GPU utilization, token generation variance, error codes (time-outs, 429s).
- Recording: store traces in the shared drive folder (link in MAP). Ensure we tag runs with run_id (VER_20261103_RUN001).
- Load profile tuning: start with 150 rps then ramp to 250 sustained then step to 400 burst for 60s windows.

I'll prepare the load_profile_samples.json and a short-run script. Also will set TTL for logs to 90 days per Veridian's request.

—Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer
[Internal only — do not forward]

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@veridianhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@veridianhealth.com>, Veridian Health - Engineering <eng@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Veridian MAP kickoff: perf scope & timelines

Evelyn — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple quick clarifying questions before we hand artifacts to our procurement/legal team:

1) For TTFT you list median <= 160ms (target) and p99 <= 250ms (target). For contract acceptance, is the stricter p99 <= 250ms the hard gate or the relaxed p99 <= 300ms in your success criteria? We need to be explicit in the MAP.
2) During the burst to 400 rps, are you expecting degraded quality or elevated error rates? If so, please document the fallback behavior (model variant fallback, queued requests, or rate limiting).
3) Can you confirm the exact data we'll need to provide for the regression eval set? We want to make sure no PHI leaves our environment; can we provide sanitized prompts only?

If we can get those clarified, procurement can fold the playbook into the SOW and we can keep the 2026-11-12 signature target.

—Samantha
Senior Engineering Manager, Veridian Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@veridianhealth.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Veridian MAP kickoff: perf scope & timelines — final playbook & preliminary run results

Samantha / Tom — thanks for the questions. We adjusted the playbook to make the contract gates explicit and completed an initial run on a production-like staging cluster today. Summary and answers below; full CSV of run metrics attached (results_summary_20261103.csv) and we've uploaded annotated traces to the shared drive.

Answers to your questions:
1) Acceptance gate: p99 first-token <= 300ms is the hard contract gate (we recommend aiming for p99 <= 250ms as a stretch target). The playbook now states:
   - Contract SLO: p99 first-token <= 300ms in production-like environment and error rate < 1%.
   - MAP target: p99 <= 250ms, median TTFT <= 160ms.

2) Burst behavior: during our controlled 400 rps bursts we observed a transient increase in 429s when GPU queue depth hit max. Fallback policy in the playbook:
   - Step 1: short-term queuing on load balancer (max queue 2s) while autoscaler spins up.
   - Step 2: if queue exceeds threshold, gracefully downgrade to a smaller model variant for interactive routes (same prompt template) for up to 60s.
   - Step 3: if degradation continues, apply token-based rate limiting to preserve overall system health.
We observed quality delta of ~0.9% on automated evals when downgrading; that is within the 1.5% regression threshold.

3) Regression eval set: provide sanitized prompts only (no PHI). We will run evals on your sanitized set inside the staging VPC — no Veridian data leaves your environment. Required files: 1) eval_prompts_sanitized.jsonl; 2) golden_responses.jsonl (optional; we can run model-only comparisons if you cannot share gold labels).

Preliminary run results (VER_20261103_RUN001):
- Interactive profile (15-minute sustained at 250 rps): median TTFT = 150ms, p95 first-token = 180ms, p99 first-token = 220ms, error rate = 0.3%.
- Burst window (400 rps, 60s): p99 first-token spike to 480ms for the top 1% while autoscaler scaled; implemented fallback reduced observed quality by ~0.9% but prevented sustained errors.
- Batch profile: 95th percentile batch latency = 4.2s for up to 3 concurrent jobs (meets target).
- Concurrency/scale: autoscaler recovered baseline in 75s after burst (meets 90s requirement).

Conclusion: the run meets contract gates (p99 <= 300ms, error rate < 1%, throughput >= 250 rps sustained). We recommend signing the MAP with the agreed SLOs and including a 30-day post-launch monitoring window to watch for production variance.

Next steps / asks from Veridian:
- Please deliver sanitized eval_prompts_sanitized.jsonl and allowlist IPs by EOD 2026-11-04.
- Confirm procurement timeline to lock the signature date.
- Review the attached results CSV and comment in the Drive doc for any follow-up traces you'd like us to analyze.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short sync if you want to walk through the traces.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
